content: Standard correlation-adjusted exposure aggregation: pairwise portfolio variance formula var = w1^2*s1^2 + w2^2*s2^2 + 2*w1*w2*rho*s1*s2 is the rigorous basis. A simpler, widely used practitioner approximation for exposure caps: effective_exposure = sum(individual exposures) * (1 + avg_pairwise_correlation among open positions), or equivalently scale down per-position risk budget by (1 - rho) when rho is positive and high (e.g. size to 0.6% risk instead of 1% at rho=0.8 to keep combined risk near independent-equivalent 1%). Cluster-cap approach also common: cap total exposure to any correlated cluster (e.g. pairs with pairwise corr > 0.7) at a fixed ceiling (e.g. 30% of the per-pair limit summed).
